courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Elementary Portuguese I
courses.description: Introduces the essential elements of Portuguese structure and vocabulary and aspects of Brazilian and Portuguese culture. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing are stressed in that order. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 101 and PORT 111 or 401 .

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Elementary Portuguese II
courses.description: Continues study of essential elements of Portuguese structure, vocabulary, and aspects of Brazilian and Portuguese culture. Aural comprehension, speaking, reading, and writing are stressed in that order. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 102 and PORT 111 or 401 .

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Intensive Elementary Portuguese
courses.description: Covers the material of the PORT 101 and 102 sequence in a single semester. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 111 and PORT 101 , 102 , or 401 .

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Intermediate Portuguese I
courses.description: Further development of language with emphasis on speaking, writing, and a review of grammar. Includes advanced Portuguese structures, cultural and literary texts. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 203 and PORT 212 or 402 .

source.text: PORT 203. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 102 , 111 , or 401 . | GLBL-LANG.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Intermediate Portuguese II
courses.description: Continued development of language skills for communication. Further study of grammar. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 204 and PORT 212 or 402 .

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Intensive Intermediate Portuguese
courses.description: A continuation of PORT 111 ; covers the material of PORT 203 and 204 in one semester. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 212 and PORT 203 , 204 , or 402 .

source.text: PORT 212. | 6 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 102 , 111 , or 401 . | GLBL-LANG.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Reimagining Climate Futures in the Lusophone World: Narratives, Data, and Discourse
courses.description: This interdisciplinary course explores how climate change and environmental futures are imagined, narrated, and contested across the Portuguese-speaking world. Through a combination of literary texts, film, visual art, ethnographic studies, and scientific discourse, we investigate how climate change is lived, represented, and resisted in diverse Lusophone contexts, including Brazil, Mozambique, Angola, and Portugal. Taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Course Correspondent Project in Portuguese
courses.description: Learning contract required. Students participating in UNC-led study abroad programs develop activities to supplement instruction in on-campus courses. Supervised by the on-campus instructor, students file reports on the sites, language, and culture of the country in which they are studying. Pass/Fail only. Permission of the instructor and the instructor's department.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Advanced Communication in Portuguese: Media & Entertainment
courses.description: Development of speaking skills through discussion of media, popular music, and selected texts.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PORT 310. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-AESTH, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Brazilian Performance in Music and Dance: Capoeira
courses.description: Study of Brazilian capoeira from its roots to the present day. Focus on verbal and nonverbal discourse experienced through the rules, songs, movements, rhythms, rituals of capoeira. In English; credit for major/minor in Portuguese if readings and written work are done in Portuguese.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Advanced Communication in Portuguese: History, Nature, and Society
courses.description: Emphasizes the learning of Portuguese through cultural context. Language, society, and miscegenation will be approached through texts and films. Focus on important aspects of religion, festivities, and popular music from the Portuguese-speaking countries of three continents.

source.text: PORT 323. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402 . | FC-PAST.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese Interpretation I
courses.description: Introduces the profession of interpreter: main interpretation models, history and theory, use of cognitive processes in developing skills, ethical standards, and best practices. Emphasis on expanding communicative and cultural competency while applying strategies in business, conference interpretation, education, health care, and law enforcement.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese Interpretation II
courses.description: Refines interpretation skills through continued study of theory and best practices in varied professional contexts. Focuses on enhancing linguistic competence, sight-translation, and mnemonic strategies. Increases cultural sensitivity to issues interpreters face in business, conference interpretation, education, health care, the hospitality industry, law, and social services.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese Translation I
courses.description: Introduction to translation theory, history and methods, and the basic elements of Portuguese-to-English and English-to-Portuguese translation through a variety of prose styles. Upon completion, students should be able to demonstrate usage and understanding of the elementary processes involved in translating.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese Translation II
courses.description: Refines translation skills in cultural and consumer-oriented, financial, legal, literary, medical, and technical domains. Emphasis on expanding written proficiency and refining style, translating representative texts from diverse populations in the United States and in Portuguese-speaking countries, and demonstrating advanced lexical and grammatical proficiency in Portuguese.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Modern Brazil through Literature and Film in Translation
courses.description: This course is devoted to the study of Brazilian culture and history through representative works of the late 19th- and early 20th-century literature with supplemental films. Taught in English. Available for major/minor credit in Portuguese if readings and written work are done in Portuguese.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese and Brazilian Fiction in Translation
courses.description: The study of selected literary works by major writers from Portugal, Brazil, and the former Portuguese colonies in Africa.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Women Writers: Brazil and Beyond
courses.description: Trajectory of women writers of the Portuguese-speaking world, with main focus on texts of the 20th and 21st century. Analysis of works within a social-historical and literary context.

source.text: PORT 382. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | WGST 381 .

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Verbal Art, Identities, and Nation in Portuguese-Speaking Africa
courses.description: Study of representative works of literature, oral tradition, popular music, and film from Lusophone Africa from the Age of Exploration through independence to the present. Focus on literary analysis, sociohistorical context, and cultures. Taught in English. Available for major/minor credit in Portuguese if readings and written work are done in Portuguese.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Brazilian Religious Movements through Film and Literature
courses.description: Literary and cinematic representations of Candomblé, Sebastianism, Positivism, and Spiritism from late-19th through the 20th century. Focus on the penetration these forms of religiosity into mainstream Brazilian culture. Taught in English; credit for Portuguese major/minor if readings and work done in Portuguese.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese, Brazilian, and African Identity in Film
courses.description: Study of the literary and cultural film production of the Portuguese-speaking world on three continents. Films in Portuguese with English subtitles.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: PORT 388. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Afrofuturism in Brazil and in the African Diaspora
courses.description: This course will study Brazil and Afrofuturism in the context of race and intersectionality and the significance of envisioning Black identity in the modern African Diaspora. Its format includes lectures, in-class groups, plenary discussions, activities outside the classroom (The Ackland Museum), workshops (Combative room), and student presentations. It is taught in English.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Research for Advanced Students
courses.description: Required preparation, two major-level courses or permission of the instructor. A tutorial for advanced students in Portuguese on a topic agreed upon by the student and a member of the faculty.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Independent Study in Portuguese
courses.description: Independent study on a selected topic in Luso-Brazilian literature and culture agreed upon by the student and a member of the faculty.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Portuguese
courses.description: A seminar on a previously announced subject.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Beginning Accelerated Brazilian Portuguese I
courses.description: Covers levels one and two of the basic language sequence in one semester. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Intensive approach to developing all skills but with an emphasis on speaking. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 401 and PORT 101 , 102 , 105 or 111 .

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Intermediate Accelerated Brazilian Portuguese II
courses.description: A continuation of PORT 401 , covers levels three and four in one semester. Develops all skills, with increasing emphasis on reading, writing, and cultural analysis. Designed for highly motivated undergraduate/graduate language learners, especially those who have experienced success with learning another language. Prepares students for advanced courses. Students may not receive credit for both PORT 402 and PORT 203 , PORT 204 or PORT 212 .

source.text: PORT 402. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 102 , 111 , or 401 . | GLBL-LANG.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: LAC Recitation
courses.description: A recitation section or stand-alone course for selected courses that promote foreign language proficiency across the curriculum (LAC). Weekly discussion and readings in Portuguese. Co-registration required unless a stand-alone LAC course; contact instructor or view Notes to determine.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

source.text: PORT 408. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese Language and Culture for the Professions
courses.description: Training for effective oral and written communication in the professional world. Builds upon linguistic and sociolinguistic concepts, refining language and enhancing cultural proficiency through extensive writing and speaking practice. Vocabulary, readings, and activities relate to social issues, business professions, and the workplace.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

source.text: PORT 420. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-GLOBAL, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Survey of Portuguese Literature I
courses.description: An introduction to Portuguese literature from its origins through the 18th century.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Climate Change and the Cultural Imagination: Lusophone Interpretations
courses.description: In this course we will explore how contemporary Lusophone culture broaches the challenges and global dynamics of climate change. How do the arts imagine solutions for the problems of contemporary environments? How might they subvert traditional configurations of knowledge and of power, and how can they impact human behavior? How might they help us envision a different future for our planet? Conducted in Portuguese.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 310, or 323; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PORT 520. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 310 , or 323 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Contemporary Portuguese Culture and Contexts
courses.description: This course examines contemporary Portuguese culture and national identity--contrasting it with European culture in general--and examining the historical events (primarily from the 20th century) that have had the greatest impact on national identity. The Estado Novo dictatorship, the 1974 Carnation Revolution, loss of the Portuguese African colonies, integration into the European Union, and the changing social perceptions of the role of women are all examined.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: History of the Portuguese Language
courses.description: Survey of the history of Portuguese with stress on the characteristics of Brazilian Portuguese and the factors underlying them.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 402; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: PORT 526. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PORT 402 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Varieties of Portuguese
courses.description: Introduction to the linguistic analysis of Portuguese. Basic linguistic comparison of Portuguese dialects at different levels of linguistic structure. Emphasis on theoretical background in understanding language variation as a property of natural languages.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Brazilian Drama
courses.description: A study of representative Brazilian plays of the 20th century with a review of the development of the theater in Brazil.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 402; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Cultural Topics from the Lusophone World
courses.description: This course examines trends in the cultural production of the Lusophone world from the 19th century to the present, including philosophy, art, film, music, and social practices in Portugal, Brazil, and Lusophone Africa. Topics may include artistic movements, race, class, gender, colonialism, and religion.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, PORT 204 or 402; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: Required of all students reading for honors. Preparation of an essay under the direction of a faculty member. Topic to be approved by thesis director in consultation with honors advisor.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Honors Thesis in Portuguese
courses.description: Restricted to senior honors candidates. Second semester of senior honors thesis. Thesis preparation under the direction of a departmental faculty member.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Advanced Composition for Graduate Students
courses.description: Advanced grammar with exercises in translation from English into Portuguese. Free composition and training in the use of stylistic devices.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Luso-Brazilian Bibliography and Methodology
courses.description: An introduction to bibliography and methodology in Luso-Brazilian literary and linguistic research.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: The Portuguese Novel
courses.description: A study of prose fiction, particularly from the 19th and 20th centuries, with special emphasis on Camilo Castelo Branco, Eça de Queirós, Aquilino Ribeiro, Ferreira de Castro, and the neo-realistas.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: The Brazilian Novel
courses.description: Extensive reading of representative Brazilian novels from the second half of the 19th century to the present.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Machado de Assis
courses.description: A study of the prose fiction, drama, poetry, and criticism of Machado de Assis, with reference to other major writers of the second half of the 19th century.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Modern Brazilian Short Fiction and Essays
courses.description: A study of Brazilian short stories, novelas, and essays of the 20th century.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Old Portuguese
courses.description: A study of Portuguese historical phonology and morphology with readings from medieval verse and prose.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Camões
courses.description: The works of Camões (epic, lyric poetry, and drama) are studied with reference to the contemporary Iberian historical and literary background.

courses.subject: PORT
courses.title: Portuguese Overseas Language and Literature
courses.description: A survey of the use and characteristics of Portuguese as used in Africa and Asia (especially Cape Verde creole) and readings from contemporary African authors using Portuguese.
